title: 01 · Server & simulation
intro: Commands run on the university EDA server after you log in. The setup file belongs to this course; it is not a universal Synopsys installer.

cards.title: Load the course environment
cards.code:
tcsh
source ~/EE5327.cshrc
which vcs
which dc_shell
cards.meaning: Enter tcsh, then load the course’s paths and environment. There is a space after source.
cards.check: Both which commands resolve to the expected installed tools. A prompt often changes from $ to %, but prompts are configurable.
cards.ask: Why can a tool work in one terminal and be missing in another?

cards.title: Build the simulation
cards.code: vcs -full64 -Mupdate -debug_access+all -kdb fa_st.v fa_gate.v
cards.meaning: -full64 selects a 64-bit build. -Mupdate supports incremental builds. -debug_access+all enables broad debug access. -kdb generates the debug database for Verdi integration.
cards.check: The log shows the intended top/testbench, no fatal errors, and a newly built simv. A successful compile is not a passing test.
cards.ask: What is the difference between parsing RTL, elaborating instances, and executing a simulation?
cards.note: These switches come from the organizer’s lab notes. Use vcs -help for your installed release. Add -sverilog when compiling SystemVerilog.

cards.title: Run and inspect
cards.code:
./simv
# Or start the configured debug GUI:
./simv -gui
cards.meaning: simv executes the compiled simulation. The GUI option opens the configured debugger; the course uses Verdi.
cards.check: Advance simulation time, add relevant signals, and verify clock/reset plus the failing transaction. Inspect the testbench PASS/FAIL result.
cards.ask: If the waveform is flat, how do you distinguish missing stimulus, stopped simulation, and missing signal capture?

sources: Organizer-provided server / VCS command notes; Labs 1–2 were not attached.

title: 02 · Libraries & setup
intro: DC stands for Design Compiler. Synthesis maps your RTL to technology cells; it does not finish placement, routing, or physical signoff.

cards.title: Tell DC where and what to use
cards.code:
set_app_var search_path [concat $search_path ./rtl ./libs]
set_app_var target_library "N16ADFP_StdCelltt0p8v25c_ccs.db"
set_app_var link_library "* N16ADFP_StdCelltt0p8v25c_ccs.db dw_foundation.sldb"
define_design_lib WORK -path ./work
cards.meaning: search_path locates files. target_library provides mapping cells. link_library resolves referenced designs/cells; * includes designs already in memory. WORK stores analyzed HDL data.
cards.check: Use the exact .synopsys_dc.setup spelling. Check library loading messages and unresolved references after link.
cards.ask: Why can a library be in link_library but not target_library?
cards.note: The N16 name is from the course. Library files are not included. DesignWare availability depends on installation/licensing.

cards.title: Read a library filename
cards.meaning: .db is Synopsys’s compiled library format. In this course name, tt indicates typical NMOS/PMOS, 0p8v means 0.8 V, 25c means 25 °C, and ccs denotes Composite Current Source modeling.
cards.check: Inspect the library’s actual units, cells, and characterization. A filename alone is not signoff evidence.
cards.ask: What information is in a timing library that is not in LEF—and vice versa?
cards.note: Liberty/.db describes functions and electrical models. LEF describes physical abstracts such as geometry and pin locations; neither substitutes for a foundry rule deck.

sources: Uploaded Lab 3: library setup and synthesis reference flow

title: 03 · Read, link, synthesize
intro: Keep structural checks and timing checks visible. A tool completing without errors does not prove the intended design was constrained.

cards.title: Construct the design
cards.code:
analyze -format verilog {fulladd_gate.v add4_struct.v}
elaborate add4_struct
current_design add4_struct
link
check_design
cards.meaning: Analyze reads HDL; elaborate resolves the top, parameters, and hierarchy. current_design makes the target explicit. link resolves references; check_design catches structural issues.
cards.check: No unresolved modules, unexpected black boxes, unintended latches, multiple drivers, or undriven essential signals.
cards.ask: What can elaborate catch that a syntax-only check cannot?
cards.note: Use the module names actually present in your files. Some flows link implicitly; keep explicit link and inspect its diagnostics.

cards.title: Map, inspect, and save
cards.code:
compile
report_area
report_timing
report_constraint -all_violators
check_timing
write_file -format ddc -hierarchy -output mapped.ddc
write_file -format verilog -hierarchy -output mapped.v
write_sdc mapped.sdc
start_gui
cards.meaning: Compile maps and optimizes. Reports expose the result. Save the tool database, mapped netlist, and constraints for reproducibility.
cards.check: Timing is constrained; area is plausible; the chosen libraries and ports are correct. Review the worst path, not only the headline slack.
cards.ask: Why might positive synthesis slack become negative after routing?
cards.note: A .ddc is a DC database; a .v netlist and .sdc constraints have different roles. start_gui opens DC’s GUI, not a waveform simulator.

sources: Uploaded Lab 3, synthesis flow and deliverables

title: 04 · Timing budgets
intro: Input and output delays model the surrounding system. They do not insert gates or consume a percentage of the clock automatically.

cards.title: Constrain a combinational block
cards.code:
create_clock -name CLK -period 1
set_input_delay 0.08 -clock [get_clocks CLK] [all_inputs]
set_output_delay 0.12 -clock [get_clocks CLK] [all_outputs]
cards.meaning: With no source object, CLK is virtual. For this simplified max-delay example, input arrives at 0.08 and output must arrive by 0.88: internal budget is 0.80 time units.
cards.check: Verify library time units (ns in the lab). At 0.60 output arrival, slack is 0.88 - 0.60 = +0.28 ns.
cards.ask: If 0.60 is internal delay rather than arrival time, what changes?
cards.note: For production I/O signoff specify -min and -max from external timing requirements. This simplified lab example assumes no other latency or uncertainty.

cards.title: Use a real clock on a sequential design
cards.code:
create_clock -name CLK -period 2 [get_ports clk]
set data_inputs [remove_from_collection [all_inputs] [get_ports {clk rst_n}]]
set_input_delay -max 0.20 -clock CLK $data_inputs
set_input_delay -min 0.05 -clock CLK $data_inputs
set_output_delay -max 0.25 -clock CLK [all_outputs]
set_output_delay -min -0.05 -clock CLK [all_outputs]
cards.meaning: Attach a clock to the actual port. Constrain data ports separately from the clock and reset. Negative output min delay can model positive external hold time in a simple zero-skew interface.
cards.check: These example numbers must be replaced with interface requirements. Analyze reset recovery/removal and any exceptions deliberately.
cards.ask: Why is applying data input delay to the clock port a mistake?
cards.note: Do not copy the example into an unknown design. Reset policy, clock uncertainty, generated clocks, and clock-domain relationships require separate constraints.

cards.title: Model the environment electrically
cards.code:
set_driving_cell -lib_cell BUFFD2BWP20P90 \
  -input_transition_rise 0.1 -input_transition_fall 0.1 [all_inputs]
set_load [expr {[load_of [get_lib_pins */BUFFD2BWP20P90/I]] * 4}] [all_outputs]
cards.meaning: Driving-cell modeling estimates input slew from an external cell. Output load models capacitance, here four reference input-pin loads. These are separate from I/O timing delays.
cards.check: Ensure the library pin selection is unambiguous, units match, and load is realistic. Adapt port selection for sequential designs.
cards.ask: Can a circuit meet timing with an unrealistic output load? What would that prove?

sources: Uploaded Lab 3: virtual clock, I/O delays, driving cell and load sections

title: 05 · Read reports
intro: Always identify units, corner, mode, path group, and analysis stage before drawing a conclusion.

cards.title: Ask both timing questions
cards.code:
report_timing -delay_type max
report_timing -delay_type min
report_constraint -all_violators
check_timing
cards.meaning: Max-delay analysis examines setup-style requirements; min-delay analysis examines hold-style requirements. check_timing identifies missing or inconsistent timing setup.
cards.check: Setup slack = required - arrival. Hold slack = arrival - required. Read startpoint, endpoint, clocks, cell delay, and net delay.
cards.ask: Why can lowering the clock frequency fix setup but usually not a same-edge hold failure?

cards.title: Compare methods fairly
cards.meaning: Record RTL revision, library/corner, SDC, compile recipe, area, WNS/TNS, violating endpoints, and power activity. Change one factor at a time.
cards.check: Confirm runs constrain the same paths and use the same timing/power assumptions before ranking them.
cards.ask: Would you choose lower area if it misses timing? How would you present the Pareto tradeoff?

cards.title: Lab 4 optimization directives
cards.code:
set_structure true -boolean true -timing true
compile -exact_map -boundary_optimization
cards.meaning: This is one Lab 4 recipe for timing-driven structuring with Boolean optimization. Compare against the handout’s flattening experiments in separate clean runs.
cards.check: Compare the mapped schematic and reports. Preserve a baseline; do not mix stale constraints or directives across experiments.
cards.ask: How can logic sharing save area but create a high-fanout timing bottleneck?
cards.note: Legacy commands/options depend on release. The handout’s set_flatten is logic minimization; do not confuse it with simply removing HDL hierarchy.

sources: Uploaded Lab 3: setup and hold reporting

title: 06 · FSM experiments
intro: The updated lab compares explicitly pre-encoded binary and one-hot RTL. Old extracted-FSM commands shown in background sections are not a reliable current recipe.

cards.title: Use the supported lab path
cards.code:
set_app_var fsm_auto_inferring true
set_app_var fsm_enable_state_minimization true
# Read one pre-encoded RTL variant in a clean run.
compile_ultra
report_fsm
report_area
report_timing
cards.meaning: Run the binary and one-hot variants separately with identical constraints, then inspect whether encoding was preserved and whether the FSM was recognized.
cards.check: The updated lab expects Re-Encoding style: NONE. Record state registers, area, and worst reg-to-reg slack.
cards.ask: Why might one-hot reduce decode depth but increase clock power?
cards.note: Lab 5 documents CMD-080 for set_fsm_encoding_style in syn_2022.12. Do not paste the older background FSM command chain.

cards.title: Choose based on evidence
cards.meaning: Binary uses ceil(log2(N)) state bits; one-hot typically uses N. Gray-like coding can reduce switching for selected transitions, but arbitrary FSM transitions are not all one-bit changes.
cards.check: Check illegal-state behavior, reset, output timing, and equivalent externally visible behavior for every encoding.
cards.ask: Would a safety requirement change how you handle unused encodings?

sources: Uploaded Lab 5: updated binary/one-hot RTL procedure and final questions

title: 07 · Scan & ATPG
intro: Functional verification checks behavior. Manufacturing test seeks modeled physical faults. TetraMAX is the course tool; newer flows and licenses may use different products.

cards.title: Make test intent explicit
cards.code:
set_scan_configuration -style multiplexed_flip_flop
# Declare actual clock/reset/test ports with set_dft_signal.
create_test_protocol
dft_drc -verbose
compile_ultra -scan
cards.meaning: Configure the scan style, declare test intent, build a protocol, and run pre-DFT checks. Test-ready synthesis can replace functional flops with scan-capable cells.
cards.check: Verify controllable clocks/reset and inspect unscannable registers. Scan replacement is not the same as scan-chain stitching.
cards.ask: Why can one uncontrollable reset make ATPG ineffective?
cards.note: This is a flow fragment. Supply your real scan-clock timing, active reset polarity, ports, and license-supported options.

cards.title: Stitch and recheck
cards.code:
set_dft_signal -view spec -type ScanDataIn -port test_si
set_dft_signal -view spec -type ScanDataOut -port test_so
set_dft_signal -view spec -type ScanEnable -port test_se
create_test_protocol -infer_asynch -infer_clock
dft_drc -verbose
set_scan_configuration -replace false
insert_dft
dft_drc -verbose -coverage
report_constraint -all_violators
cards.meaning: With scan-replaced flops already present, stitch the chain and recheck test rules plus functional constraints.
cards.check: Save matching pre/post-DFT netlists and protocols. Recheck functional equivalence, area, and timing after insertion.
cards.ask: What is the area and test-time tradeoff between one long chain and several shorter chains?
cards.note: The -replace false setting assumes the earlier test-ready compile already replaced eligible flops.

cards.title: Generate and analyze patterns
cards.code:
tmax -gui
# In TetraMAX, load the library models and matching netlist.
# Build the model, read the matching STIL protocol, and pass DRC.
# Select the fault model, seed faults, run ATPG, then inspect classes.
cards.meaning: Separate build, test DRC, and ATPG. Compare basic scan, fast sequential, and full sequential with controlled settings.
cards.check: Check DT, UD, AU, ND and the total. Fault coverage and test coverage use different denominators.
cards.ask: Can 100% test coverage coexist with less than 100% fault coverage?
cards.note: Lab 6 mixes stuck-at instructions with transition-fault sample reports. Record the actual chosen fault model; do not compare unlike fault models.

sources: Uploaded Lab 6: DFT insertion, TetraMAX procedure and sample coverage reports

title: 08 · Activity & power
intro: Dynamic power depends on activity, capacitance, voltage, and frequency. Leakage is a different component. A smaller reported number is meaningful only under comparable conditions.

cards.title: Describe switching honestly
cards.code:
set_switching_activity -static_probability 0.01 \
  -toggle_rate 1.5625 -period 10 [get_ports enable]
set_switching_activity -static_probability 0.5 \
  -toggle_rate 15.625 -period 10 [get_ports up]
set_switching_activity -static_probability 0.995 \
  -toggle_rate 0.015625 -period 10 [get_ports rst]
cards.meaning: The updated lab’s table gives P(0) and toggles per 10 ns. -static_probability is P(1), so convert using 1 - P(0).
cards.check: Verify design time units are ns and port names match. Inspect annotation coverage rather than assuming the activity reached every node.
cards.ask: Does 1.5625 toggles per interval imply a 1.5625 Hz frequency? Why not?
cards.note: If using a SAIF workflow beyond the lab, validate instance mapping and simulation window; reset-heavy or idle-only traces can mislead.

cards.title: Read the power evidence
cards.code:
report_power -analysis_effort high -verbose
report_saif -hier
report_threshold_voltage_group
cards.meaning: Break out internal, net switching, and leakage power. Check activity annotation and the actual cell-threshold mix.
cards.check: Compare area, timing, and power using the same corner, activity, clock period, and units.
cards.ask: If power drops but timing fails, is that an optimization success?
cards.note: The handout’s extreme clock-period experiment is optimization pressure, not proof that the circuit operates at 1 THz.

title: 09 · Clock gating & Vt
intro: Clock gating targets clock-driven switching; multi-Vt selection trades delay against leakage. Neither is free.

cards.title: Infer integrated clock gates
cards.code:
set_clock_gating_style -pos integrated -control_point before
compile_ultra -gate_clock
report_clock_gating
report_power -analysis_effort high -verbose
report_timing
cards.meaning: Use the corrected positive-edge integrated-gating style in the handout and synthesize eligible enable-controlled registers with clock gating.
cards.check: Confirm gates were inserted and which registers are covered. Check enable timing, test enable, area overhead, and post-CTS consequences.
cards.ask: Why is assign gclk = clk & enable unsafe if enable can change while clk is high?
cards.note: Exact ICG availability depends on the library. Clock-gating checks and test behavior still matter after insertion.

cards.title: Explore threshold choices
cards.code:
man set_multi_vth_constraint
report_threshold_voltage_group
cards.meaning: Use your release’s documented constraint to bound low-Vt usage; inspect whether the limit applies by count or area and whether it is hard or soft.
cards.check: Measure the achieved mix and slack. Low-Vt often speeds cells but increases leakage; high/standard-Vt can save leakage on paths with margin.
cards.ask: Why is “replace every cell with low-Vt” a poor default?
cards.note: Do not guess percentage/group option names across releases. The lab requests a 10% LVT-control experiment; reproduce the exact documented local syntax.

sources: Uploaded Lab 7: corrected gating style, Vt experiments and questions

title: 10 · Cadence counterpart
intro: Learn the operation, then its tool-specific command. Cadence Common UI and legacy UI differ; do not blindly translate a DC script.

cards.title: Simulate with Xcelium
cards.code: xrun -64bit -sv -gui dut.sv tb.sv
cards.meaning: A typical Xcelium invocation compiles, elaborates, and simulates SystemVerilog, with GUI debug.
cards.check: Use your local xrun help and record compile order, top module, seed, and debug-access settings.
cards.ask: Which parts of your testbench should stay portable between VCS and Xcelium?

cards.title: Synthesize with Genus
cards.meaning: Read timing libraries and HDL → elaborate top → read SDC → generic synthesis → technology mapping → optimization → reports and exports.
cards.check: Inspect resolved hierarchy, constraints, cell mapping, timing, and area. Use the installed Genus reference flow for exact commands.
cards.ask: Does a common SDC file guarantee identical results in DC and Genus?
cards.note: Genus uses its own library and database setup. The conceptual flow is shown here rather than an unverified, release-specific full script.

cards.title: Implement with Innovus
cards.meaning: Import netlist, technology/cell abstracts, timing views and SDC → floorplan/power plan → placement → CTS → routing → extraction/signoff feedback.
cards.check: At each checkpoint inspect timing, congestion, utilization, power connectivity, and design-rule violations.
cards.ask: Why is a clean pre-CTS setup report insufficient for signoff?
cards.note: Use Innovus/Tempus/Quantus/Voltus for related implementation, timing, extraction, and rail-analysis tasks. They are separate analyses, even when integrated.

title: 11 · Physical design methods
intro: Fix the cause exposed by the physical evidence. Do not apply the same optimization to every negative-slack path.

cards.title: Cell delay or wire delay?
cards.meaning: Cell dominated: consider sizing, Vt, logic restructuring, or pipelining when architecture allows. Wire dominated: investigate placement, fanout, buffering, layer choice, and routing detours.
cards.check: Compare the delay breakdown before/after; recheck power, hold, congestion, and all relevant corners.
cards.ask: Why might upsizing every gate make routing worse?

cards.title: Floorplan and clock choices
cards.meaning: Explore utilization, macro orientation, channels, halos, pin placement, and power-grid access. After CTS, evaluate clock latency, skew, transition, and endpoint timing.
cards.check: A floorplan with low average utilization can still have a congested macro channel. Inspect local demand.
cards.ask: When would you change the floorplan instead of accepting another timing ECO?

cards.title: Close across modes and corners
cards.meaning: Check functional/test modes, min/max timing, RC and PVT corners, crosstalk, variation, EM/IR, and physical rules. Re-extract after routing changes.
cards.check: Use a corner-by-corner comparison and record new violations; an ECO that improves one path can damage another.
cards.ask: How can useful skew help setup but hurt hold?

sources.label: Synopsys ICC II training: block implementation topics

title: 12 · Analog layout loop
intro: Analog physical design preserves electrical intent at device and interconnect level. There is no universal layout recipe independent of the circuit and PDK.

cards.title: Capture intent before placement
cards.meaning: Identify matched groups, ratios, sensitive nodes, symmetry requirements, current paths, isolation, and relevant device orientation constraints.
cards.check: Use unit devices where appropriate; compare centroid positions, environment, routing, contacts, and well proximity.
cards.ask: When might common-centroid placement be less useful than a compact, carefully routed pair?

cards.title: DRC, LVS, extraction, simulation
cards.meaning: DRC checks geometry against rules. LVS checks extracted connectivity/devices against the source. PEX extracts parasitics. Post-layout simulation checks performance with those parasitics.
cards.check: A DRC/LVS-clean block can still fail bandwidth, offset, noise, stability, or reliability requirements.
cards.ask: What would you inspect if gain barely changes after layout but phase margin collapses?

cards.title: Use corners and mismatch analysis
cards.meaning: Run appropriate process/voltage/temperature corners and statistical mismatch analysis with foundry-supported models. Compare schematic and extracted results using matched conditions.
cards.check: A corner sweep and Monte Carlo answer different questions. Track yield assumptions and sample size rather than claiming certainty from a handful of runs.
cards.ask: Can a common-centroid layout eliminate random mismatch?
cards.note: Cadence: Virtuoso, Spectre, Quantus, Pegasus/PVS. Synopsys: Custom Compiler, PrimeSim, StarRC, IC Validator. Follow the licensed PDK-qualified flow.
